messages.subject: Re: Accessing data.frame
messages.body_plain:
Donald,

On Oct 11, 2010, at 6:14 AM, Donald Winston wrote:

> 
> table.read() returns a data.frame.
> 
> How do I access a data.frame using REXP and just Java?
> 
> Or do I have to use R? Like the following:
> 
> REXP myDataFrame = c.eval("table.read(" + filename + ")");
> c.assign("df", myDataFrame);
> REXP x = c.eval("colnames(df) <- c('Gender','Age','Weight',...)");
> then I can work with x in Java.
> 

I'm not sure about your intention above -- x will be the vector of column names, not the data frame. Also which back-end are you using - JRI or Rserve? I ask because it makes more sense if myDataFrame is a reference (so you use parseAndEval("yourcode...", null, false) instead but Rserve has no references).
That said, it's much more efficient to use
REXP myDataFrame = c.eval("df<-table.read(" + filename + ")")

Also I strongly discourage the constructs like above because you get into quoting hell (if the file name contains anything special like \, quotes or unicode escapes). So you really want to use instead:
c.assign("fn", filename)
c.eval("table.read(fn)")

I'm not sure if that answers your question, but it was very vague so I'm not sure I understood what you are trying to do...

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: .jinit -Xmx parameter trouble
messages.body_plain:
On Oct 13, 2010, at 5:39 AM, Ilhami Visne wrote:

> Hello,
> 
> I need more memory than the default one 512m, so i'm calling the .jinit with -Xmx1024m parameter. I put the call (.jinit(parameters="-Xmx1024m") ) in the .First.lib function of my package (depends on rJava). But it has no effect and still initialize with 512m (checking it with Java VisualVM). 
> 

You should not need to call .jinit directly in a package - that's what .jpackage is for. Also if you want to set global parameters, you should use the "java.parameters" option (preferably before loading any packages):

options(java.parameters="-Xmx1024m")

because you have no control over who will be actually initializing the JVM so your .jinit call may not be able to honor any options. Also note that you cannot control the heap size if your R is being run by a JVM (e.g. via JGR).

Cheers,
Simon

On Oct 26, 2010, at 4:53 AM, David Richardson wrote:

> Hi,
> 
> I'm starting to use Rserve for the first time. I've set it running on a
> linux box, connecting with the java client from windows. Everything has
> been straight forward so far, I've been able to connect, run some
> commands, and get the answers I expected back.
> 
> The odd thing I've seen is that if I connect with the wrong username or
> password child processes are left running on the linux box and they
> don't seem to get cleaned up. Obviously I won't make a habit of logging
> in with the wrong credentials, but it doesn't seem ideal. I can't find
> any reference to this problem through google, I was wondering if anyone
> here can give me some pointers.
> 
> I'm running R version 2.11.1 (2010-05-31) on debian (lenny) with Rserve
> 0.6-2, with this configuration:
> 
> pwdfile /path/to/pwd.conf
> remote enable
> auth required
> plaintext disable
> interactive no
> encoding utf8
> 
> The relevant client code is below:
> 		
> RConnection rConnection = null;
> 
> try {
> 	rConnection = new RConnection(hostname,6311);
> 	if (rConnection.needLogin()){
> 		rConnection.login("notauser", "notapwd");
> 	}
> 	// do some stats
> }
> catch (RserveException e){
> 	throw new RuntimeException(e);
> }
> catch (REngineException e){
> 	throw new RuntimeException(e);
> }
> catch (REXPMismatchException e){
> 	throw new RuntimeException(e);
> }
> finally {
> 	if (rConnection != null) {
> 		rConnection.close();
> 	}
> }
> 
>> From debugging, rConnection.login is invoked, an RserveException is
> caught and rConnection.close() is called, but the child process is left
> running on the server.
> 		
> Many thanks,
> 
> Dave		
> 
> --
